summary: The recorded base reproduces both issue mechanisms: fixed simulated acceptance writes token id 100, while complete replacement-character output remains uncommitted and replacement streams leave an unbounded decode window. At the exact candidate commit, the authored regressions, independent UTF-8 boundary cases, deterministic content-equivalence fuzzing, and the gfx950 simulated-acceptance tensor check all pass. The Python source changes cover EAGLE, NGRAM, and DFlash and preserve incomplete UTF-8 suffixes while committing complete U+FFFD output. No remaining source-level counterexample was found.

tests.what_was_measured: Recorded-base behavior using the candidate regression fixture: 4 failed and 4 passed. Complete UTF-8 U+FFFD and a literal replacement token emitted empty strings; long replacement streams remained uncommitted and unbounded.
The recorded base filled predict with [100, 100, 100, 100], reproducing the benchmark-path hardcoded-token defect.
Exact candidate regressions: 11 passed, including the two prior-review counterexamples, immediate complete-U+FFFD commits, bounded oversized events, and tokenizer-derived simulated tokens.

tests.command: candidate deterministic adversarial UTF-8 content-equivalence script
tests.what_was_measured: 335 seeded random byte streams across lengths 1 through 4096 and randomized event splits matched Python's independent bytes.decode(errors='replace') reference after a clean flush; every decode window remained below 64 tokens. Targeted 2-, 3-, and 4-byte scalars crossing the recovery threshold also passed.
Expanded candidate regression and adjacent stop-trimming suite: 19 passed.
On AMD Instinct MI350X gfx950, synchronized device tensors produced predict [64, 64, 64, 64] and num_correct_drafts [2].

The reported eight-GPU TP8/DP8/EAGLE serving topology and 16,384-request throughput/TTFT experiment were unavailable; performance recovery at that scale remains unmeasured here.
